scores.evidence: metrics.json has no hard failures: overflowX false, 0 console errors, 0 mermaid errors, 0 unknown blocks and 0 broken images. The hook-loop flowchart (Fig. 1) is TD with Japanese labels that can be read at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-04.png). Term tables, the exit-code table, the scope table and the A/B comparison tables fit the 390 px width and nothing is clipped (pages/mobile-jp-13.png, mobile-jp-16.png, mobile-jp-25.png, mobile-jp-26.png).

No screen is text-only on either device (textOnlyScreens is empty). Every section alternates a term table, code and a check. The lesson is long, though: 34 mobile screens and 24 desktop screens. The practice section stacks a prompt, a 19-line script and a 24-line settings.json back to back (pages/mobile-jp-22.png to mobile-jp-24.png), which is the densest stretch.

This is a JP-only lesson. All UI and diagram labels are in Japanese, and English appears only as glossed terms and code. Contrast is good everywhere, including the callouts and the dark code blocks. No control is hidden under the 56 px top bar or the 60 px bottom bar on mobile (pages/mobile-jp-30.png, mobile-jp-34.png). No personal data appears on any screen: the desktop rail shows only an EN/JP language switch, with no account name or email.

niceToHave: Desktop JP charsPerLine median is 42 (max 53), just above the 30–40 target at a 680 px measure. This comes from the reader's measure, not from the lesson text (reader:).

reader: on mobile the header of the practice script's code block truncates the filename to '.claude/hooks/protect-files....' (pages/mobile-jp-22.png). The full path appears in the step text above and on desktop, but the header could wrap or use a smaller font.

reader: in the settings.json blocks, the long 'command' value soft-wraps inside the word 'hoo/ks' at 390 px (pages/mobile-jp-09.png, mobile-jp-23.png), and on desktop it breaks at 'block-/rm.sh' (pages/desktop-jp-07.png). It still reads correctly with the hanging indent. If the lesson wants to avoid it, it could shorten the path, for example by naming the hook directory 'hooks/' relative to $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in prose only.

reader: the inline chip '"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/block-rm.sh' in step 2 of 8-2 is longer than the mobile line and wraps inside its box (pages/mobile-jp-10.png), as does the protect-files path chip (pages/mobile-jp-22.png). Both are readable, and the same value appears in the code block.

reader: the A and B comparison tables in the practice section use different first-column widths on desktop (pages/desktop-jp-18.png), which makes side-by-side scanning slightly harder. A fixed label-column width for key/value tables would align them.

reader: environment noise, not lesson defects. 14 /api/ requests failed (500 on user progress, events and notifications); the end banner says this is the course's last lesson because drafts are not in course.json (pages/mobile-jp-34.png, desktop-jp-24.png); and both full-length PNGs are truncated.
summary: Visually clean on both mobile (390 px) and desktop. There are no hard failures in metrics.json, the hook-loop diagram and every table can be read at 390 px, there is no personal data on any screen, and every section has a table, code or a check. The only rough spots come from the reader: long path chips and command lines wrap inside the path, and one code-block filename is truncated on mobile. All of these are listed as nice-to-have.
